feat(runtime): serve 404/5xx/root-redirect in Hono; drop Traefik plugin

Moves 404, 5xx, and root-redirect responsibilities from Traefik into the
app so the workflow-engine image is self-contained. Collapses the main
IngressRoute to a single catch-all and deletes the inline-response plugin
scaffolding (init container, ConfigMap, vendored tarball).

Global `app.notFound` + `app.onError` in createApp branch on `Accept:
text/html`; sub-apps (`/api`, `/trigger`, `/dashboard`) install the same
shared factory because Hono sub-apps mounted via `app.use` don't bubble
their 404s to the parent. New `error.html` mirrors `404.html` (linked
stylesheet, plain link, CSP-clean); `error.css` folded into
`workflow-engine.css` under `body.error-page` scoping.

OpenSpec: self-contained-app-image. 822/822 tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(ui): prepare dashboard + trigger for strict CSP

Swap alpinejs/dist/cdn.min.js -> @alpinejs/csp. Register every Alpine
component via Alpine.data(...) so HTML expressions reduce to bare
identifiers and single method calls. Move multi-statement bodies and
global access (clearTimeout, JSON.parse, navigator.clipboard) into
component methods, where the CSP evaluator does not reach. Convert
:style bindings to object form so Alpine sets styles via
setProperty (CSP-safe) instead of attribute writes (blocked).

Extract inline <style> blocks from trigger/page.ts and static/404.html
into external stylesheets. Replace static style="" with classes and
dynamic color attrs with data-color selectors in workflow-engine.css.

Replace ontoggle/onclick inline handlers on the trigger page with
addEventListener wiring in trigger-forms.js, passing the event name
via data-event-type on the submit button.

New html-invariants.test.ts locks in CSP-safe rendering: no inline
<script>/<style>/on*=/style= across every HTML surface, every x-data
is a bare identifier, every :style is object form.

No response-header changes yet; those land in the follow-up once the
UI is confirmed CSP-ready. Part of openspec change add-security-headers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: add custom 404/5xx error pages and reorganize Traefik routing

Replace per-route opt-in auth model with explicit whitelists (auth,
no-auth, app-auth) and a deny-by-default catch-all. Unknown paths now
show a styled 404 page served from the app's static assets. 5xx errors
are handled via a Traefik self-loopback using the traefik_inline_response
plugin on an internal HTTP entrypoint, so the error page renders even
when the app is erroring.

New routes: /livez (public), /api/* (app-auth), /* catch-all (404).
New middlewares: not-found (404), server-error (5xx), inline-error (plugin).

Real-world test against qwen2.5:14b on the Marshall Fire transcript
exposed two bugs: the duplicate-call detector only caught identical
consecutive calls (so add_resource("Claimant") with different args
slipped through), and an Ollama edge case returned an empty assistant
turn that crashed the loop. Added a `duplicate_name` check per primitive
kind and a tolerance for empty assistant content. Tightened the layered
system prompt with mandatory phase ordering (nouns → memberships →
operations → tasks → processes → triggers/rules → finalize), explicit
naming examples, and a guard against early finalize.

spec into openspec/specs/.

Member web app (Cookbook) + admin SPA — the web-app plan, end to end (#209)

* Member web app + admin SPA consolidation solution plan

Working plan for an orchestrator agent: one SPA stack (React 19, TanStack
Query/Router, shadcn/ui, PWA/offline) for the member app and the admin
rewrite, first-party cookie sessions on the existing invite machinery, a
per-area typed /api surface over the existing throw-free src/ operations,
and the deterministic backend lifts (propose interaction extensions,
recipe-to-grocery expansion, identity-graph substitutions, aisle capture).
Phased for autonomous execution; design source remains the Claude Design
project.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CLdUFxqUguFmpLnLbG668S

* Plan revisions: ETags, build-version skew check, derived to-buy flow

Go-all-the-way conditional requests (weak ETags + 304s on reads, If-Match
on whole-document writes, canonical-id LWW upserts kept If-Match-free so
offline replay never 412s), a build-version header + /api/version endpoint
for skew-triggered update prompts, and W2 reframed: no discrete
plan-to-list expansion — computeToBuy's derivation becomes a first-class
read (virtual menu rows on the grocery view) and both the agent and the
app converge on derive → make cart → substitutions. Playwright wording
hardened to blocking-from-P0. Commits the extracted design bundle at
docs/plans/web-app-design/ for the plan's lifecycle.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CLdUFxqUguFmpLnLbG668S

community-supported, re-evaluated per phase) with current picks: Vite on
the Rolldown core, SWC/Oxc transforms, Tailwind v4 Oxide, Oxlint + Biome
for the new packages; tsc/Vitest/Playwright stay until native successors
are production-stable.

Extract the ingest endpoint's fixed-window KV limiter into src/rate-limit.ts
(underRateLimit(kv, key, max, windowS, now), fail-open) — ingest keeps its
exact keys/behavior via a thin wrapper, tests untouched. Add src/session.ts:

__Host-session cookie helpers, and requireSession — cookie → KV → the same

* member-app-foundations 2: the /api mount — session area, shared middleware, revocation purge

Mount the member JSON API at /api (src/api/app.ts, dispatched before /admin):

shared skeleton lands once — per-route TOOL_AE usage points (api:<METHOD>

paths), the CSRF guard (X-App-Csrf + Sec-Fetch-Site on all non-GET/HEAD),

The session area: POST login (IP-rate-limited 10/min via src/rate-limit.ts,
uniform 401 — no unknown-vs-revoked oracle), whoami through the shared weak-
ETag/If-None-Match helper, DELETE logout. GET /api/version returns the
deploy-stamped build (env.APP_BUILD, 'dev' unstamped). revoke() additionally
scans session:* and purges the member's web sessions.

* refactor(pagination): implement decorator pattern for Pageable translation

Refactors Pageable translation to use Decorator pattern instead of separate utility class.

Changes:
- Created TranslatedPageable decorator with static translate() method
  - Uses Decorator pattern: wraps Pageable with translated sort orders
  - API: TranslatedPageable.translate(original, translationMap)
  - Replaces PageableSortTranslator utility class
- Removed EventSortTranslator from EventController (unnecessary identity mapping)
  - JSON DTO fields match domain properties exactly
  - Simplified controller to pass Pageable directly to service layer
- Updated EventRepositoryAdapter to use TranslatedPageable.translate()
- Added comprehensive unit tests (8 test cases)
  - Single sort property translation
  - Multiple sort orders
  - Unknown property fallback (fail-safe)
  - Null handling preservation
  - Empty sort handling
  - Pagination parameters preservation
  - Pageable navigation methods (next, previous, first)
  - Type checking

Benefits:
- Cleaner API: TranslatedPageable.translate(pageable, map) vs PageableSortTranslator.translate()
- Better pattern alignment: Decorator pattern for wrapper functionality
- Single responsibility: TranslatedPageable handles both wrapping and translation
- Reduced duplication: 110 lines of duplicate PageableRequest removed
- Better testability: 8 focused unit tests for translation logic

**Goal**: Promote `versioning.createVersion` from naive insert to a parent-linked chain that records `parent_version_id`, enforces the status enum (`draft → approved | rejected | published`), routes serialized bodies >256KB through R2 (flag-gated), and exposes a line-level diff between two versions of the same artifact.

- Document rate limiting and lockout in .env.example, .env.development, .env.production.example

- Fix pre-existing e2e i18n test paths (wrong /api/user/register -> /auth/register)

Simplify electron bootstrap derived state (#18)

* feat(electron): simplify bootstrap to derived state (LaunchSource V2)

Implements OpenSpec change `simplify-electron-bootstrap-derived-state`.
Replaces stored startup decisions (`mode.json`, `isFirstRun`,
`decideStartupAction`) with derived-on-launch capability probes plus an
explicit `DASHBOARD_STARTER` env var stamped on every server spawn.

New capabilities
- electron-launch-source: discriminated `LaunchSource` resolver across
  attach / devMonorepo / piExtension / npmGlobal / extracted, with
  `DASHBOARD_PREFER_SOURCE` override.
- electron-bundle-extract: version-marker-driven extraction of
  `~/.pi-dashboard/`, config migration to `~/.pi/dashboard/migrate/<ts>/`,
  and the `node|node-pending|node-old` survive-extract whitelist.
- dashboard-starter-identity: `DASHBOARD_STARTER` env contract,
  `/api/health.starter` + `/api/health.pid` exposure, lifecycle ownership
  rule "only the starter, with pid match, may stop on quit".
- installable-list: `~/.pi/dashboard/installable.json` schema +
  server-side reconcile in `bootstrap-install-from-list.ts` (no-op when
  file absent).

Removed
- first-run-wizard capability: `mode.json`, `isFirstRun`,
  `decideStartupAction`, `runPowerUserManagedInstall` deletions deferred
  to a follow-up change once `LAUNCH_SOURCE_V2=false` legacy path is
  retired.
- NSIS installer + portable .exe: ZIP is now the sole Windows
  distribution (cross-platform reproducible from Docker).

Phase C bring-up fixes (Windows ZIP)
- launch-source.ts: extract from `<resourcesPath>/server`, not bare
  `resourcesPath` (top-level contains app.asar, recursive cpSync ENOTDIRs
  on opendir).
- launch-source.ts: extraction error log now includes
  code/syscall/path/message so failing entry is identifiable.
- docker-make.sh: replace every workspace symlink under
  `node_modules/@blackbelt-technology/*`, not a hardcoded subset
  (previously missed `dashboard-plugin-runtime`, dangling symlink tripped
  ENOTDIR on Windows first-launch cpSync).
- build-windows-zip.sh: anonymous Docker volume on
  `/build/packages/electron/out` to dodge Docker Desktop FUSE/VirtioFS
  EACCES on read-after-write; `--platform linux/amd64` pinned on build
  and run; `--name` + `docker cp` artifact extraction.

Supersedes
- electron-startup-splash (archived)
- electron-wizard-smart-detection (archived)

* test(electron): real-fs smoke for LaunchSource V2 + fix bootstrap regressions

Adds a tiered real-fs smoke test for the `extracted` source path that
catches the class of bugs unit tests can't see (pure mocks miss
real-fs/npm/spawn behavior). Fixes three production regressions
the smoke test surfaced.

New test file
- packages/electron/src/lib/__tests__/launch-source.smoke.test.ts
  - Tier A (always when bundle present, ~2s): real `extractBundle` over
    the host's `resources/server/`; pins layout + cliPath presence + no
    absolute symlinks.
  - Tier B (when offline cache + bundled node also present, ~30s):
    `selectLaunchSource({ preferOverride: "extracted" })` end-to-end;
    pins pi-coding-agent install, cliPath survival, jiti resolution.
  - Tier C (when host node-pty prebuild matches, ~10s): real `node
    --import <jiti> <cliPath>` spawn; pins /api/health = starter:Electron.
  - Skips cleanly with explicit reasons when prerequisites absent;
    fresh-clone friendly.

Production fixes uncovered by the smoke test

1. cpSync rewrites relative symlinks as absolute paths (Node quirk)
   - Repro: `fs.cpSync(src, dst, { recursive: true, dereference: false })`
     on a relative symlink writes an absolute path pointing at the build
     host's source tree. Users see a broken cliPath after extraction.
   - Fix: bundle-server.mjs materializes every workspace symlink under
     `@blackbelt-technology/*` before forge packs the bundle. Mirrors
     what docker-make.sh already does (Linux/Windows build paths) but
     covers native-macOS builds (build-installer.sh path) too.

2. npm install --prefix reconciles node_modules and prunes the bundle
   - Repro: with the bundle's package.json declaring no deps,
     `npm install --prefix <managedDir> @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent` wipes
     every existing node_modules/@blackbelt-technology/* AND every server
     runtime dep (fastify, node-pty, ws, ...). Stripping `workspaces` and
     deleting package-lock didn't help; the reconciliation rules vary by
     npm version.
   - Fix: swap-aside in resolveExtracted. Move
     <managedDir>/node_modules → <managedDir>/.bundle-node-modules,
     run installStandalone (npm builds a fresh tree containing only
     pi+tsx+openspec deps), then cpSync the stash back over node_modules.
     Bundle wins on conflicts (it's the version the server was tested
     against. Mostly additive merge because pi's namespace
     (@mariozechner/*) doesn't overlap with bundle deps.

3. installStandalone was missing from V2 (re-affirmed)
   - Smoke test pins that runtime baseline install runs after
     extractBundle, before any spawn would resolve jiti.

OpenSpec proposal updates
- design.md: new Bundle source path / Workspace symlink materialization
  / Runtime baseline install (jiti chicken-and-egg) / Swap-aside pattern
  sections.
- tasks.md: §13 Phase C bring-up tasks 13.1–13.8 (impl) + 13.9 (QA).

Compatibility
- No API/wire changes.
- managedDir layout: now contains a transient
  during the swap-aside; cleaned up on the same tick.
- Migration: none. Phase C hasn't shipped to users yet.
- Rollback: revert this commit + the parent feat commit.
EOF
)

* test(electron): clean-Ubuntu Docker test for V2 LaunchSource bootstrap

Modernizes packages/electron/scripts/test-electron-install{,-inner}.sh
to drive the Phase C V2 path on clean Ubuntu 22.04 instead of the
legacy tsx-wizard flow.

Stages (23 assertions, ~3 min cold):
  1. Verify bundled resource layout (Node, npm, server bundle, cliPath,
     offline cacache, node-pty linux-x64 prebuild, no abs symlinks).
  2. extractBundle (cp -a) into ~/.pi-dashboard/.
  3. Strip workspaces field from package.json + delete bundle's lockfile.
  4. Swap-aside node_modules → .bundle-node-modules.
  5. npm install --prefix --cache from offline cacache (pi+tsx+openspec
     pinned via offline-packages/manifest.json).
  6. Merge .bundle-node-modules back; verify cliPath + jiti both present.
  7. Spawn node --import <jiti-register> <cliPath>.
  8. curl /api/health within 120s; assert starter==Electron.

What this catches that the host smoke can't:
  - Linux glibc-linked node-pty native module.
  - clean-Ubuntu npm reconciliation (vs host npm version).
  - non-root user permissions.
  - bundled Node v22.18.0 (production pin) instead of host's Node.

Drops legacy assertions:
  - tsx-wizard flow / mode.json write (V2 deletes mode.json).
  - Per-package CJS/ESM checks (no longer relevant to V2 path).
  - Direct pi spawn tests (covered by other tests).

OpenSpec tasks 13.10–13.13 added documenting the test artifacts and
the production fixes they pin (smoke + Docker variants).

* test(qa): Windows VM bootstrap test for V2 LaunchSource ZIP

Adds qa/tests/07-electron-bootstrap-v2.ps1 invoked by
qa/tests/run-all.ps1 inside a Packer-built Windows VM. Drives the
production PI-Dashboard-win32-x64.zip end-to-end:

  1. Verify resources layout (server bundle, cliPath, offline cacache,
     bundled node.exe).
  2. Extract ZIP to C:\PI-Dashboard-test\.
  3. Launch pi-dashboard.exe.
  4. Poll /api/health (default port 8000) up to 180s.
  5. Assert starter==Electron, version present.
  6. Verify ~\.pi-dashboard\.version, @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent
     installation, and cliPath survival post-install (the swap-aside
     pattern from launch-source.ts).
  7. Clean up: stop process, remove extract dir.

Skips with a clear message when the ZIP artifact is absent so the
test suite still passes on VMs without a fresh build.

qa/scripts/run-test.sh: optional ZIP upload step. Looks for
packages/electron/out/make/zip/x64/PI-Dashboard-win32-x64.zip by
default, scp's to C:\qa-artifacts\ before running tests. Override
location via QA_ELECTRON_ZIP env var.

qa/README.md updated with the new test description and ZIP upload
instructions.

OpenSpec task 13.14 added documenting the qa artifact and what it
catches that Linux Docker can't see (Windows path semantics: drive
letters, junction points, \ vs /).

* chore(build): purge stale NSIS references from Docker build scripts

NSIS was removed earlier (forge.config.ts maker entry + package.json
devDep, per openspec change simplify-electron-bootstrap-derived-state),
but the build scripts still advertised it in help text, banners, and
inline comments. The Docker entrypoint also accepted ZIP_ONLY=1 from
its callers but ignored the flag.

build-installer.sh:
  - Header comment: Windows artifacts now described as
    .zip + portable .exe (not '.exe (NSIS)').
  - --help: dropped (NSIS) parenthetical from --windows. --windows-zip
    described as 'no portable' (was 'no NSIS, no portable').
  - Plan-banner line: split into two states reflecting whether
    --windows-zip is in effect.
  - Docker build comment: rationale rewritten without mentioning
    NSIS/makensis (the real reason is x64 native module ABI).

docker-make.sh:
  - Forge package step comment: explains we use forge for packaging
    only and produce ZIP via 'zip' + optional portable via
    electron-builder. Drops 'NSIS can't run on Linux' framing.
  - Portable-exe step now honors ZIP_ONLY=1: skips the
    electron-builder invocation and emits a single skip line.
    Previously the env var was passed but ignored, so --windows and
    --windows-zip produced identical output.

No production code paths touched; ZIP / portable artifacts produced
when ZIP_ONLY=0 are byte-identical to before.

* openspec: add automate-windows-remote-qa change

Adds proposal, design, specs, and tasks for a remote-Windows QA harness
under qa/remote/. Drives a real Windows host on the LAN over OpenSSH;
covers three artifact modes (ZIP, portable.exe, npm-global); reuses the
existing qa/tests/*.ps1 suite; idempotent clean-state via process kill,
port reclaim, AppData removal, portable extract-dir glob, and PID/log
cleanup. Purely additive — no production code changes.

4/4 artifacts complete; openspec validate --strict passes.

* fix(build-windows): skip electron-builder code-signing pass

No Windows certificate is configured, but electron-builder's default
CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=true causes it to attempt signing anyway,
which on Linux/Docker shells out to osslsigncode and rewrites the
entire ~169 MB portable.exe SFX (and elevate.exe) for no benefit.

- docker-make.sh: add "signtoolOptions": null to the inline JSON
  config and export CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false / WIN_CSC_LINK=
  / CSC_LINK= before the npx call.
- build-windows-zip.sh: prefix the npx call with the same env vars
  (the heredoc-config trick isn't available there; the CLI flag form
  --config.win.signtoolOptions=null would pass the string "null"
  via yargs, so env vars are used instead).

Effect: the '• signing with signtool.exe' lines disappear and the
portable build no longer pays the full PE rewrite cost on slow
Docker-on-macOS bind mounts.

* docs(simplify-electron-bootstrap): document Windows-ZIP build-script hardening

Append a Build-Script Hardening section to the proposal and a new task
group (Section 14) documenting the host-side macOS → Docker cross-compile
fixes that were required to make the Windows ZIP build pipeline pass
Phase C task 11.2 (cross-platform smoke).

Covers:
- xattr stripping before Docker (com.apple.quarantine → Linux EACCES).
- Rollup/SWC Linux-arch optional-dep top-up without wiping host variants.
- Stripping test/lint configs and *.tsbuildinfo from the runtime bundle.
- Stale out/ artifact cleanup at script entry.
- New build-windows-zip.sh script as the single Windows-ZIP entry point.

Documentation only — no code changes in this commit.

* fix(electron/doctor): escape Windows paths in launch test snippet

Doctor's server launch test embeds the CLI path in a tsx -e "import '<path>'"
snippet but only escaped single quotes. On Windows, paths like
C:\Users\user\... contain \u sequences that JS parses as unicode escapes,
causing esbuild to fail with 'Syntax error "s"' — a false-positive
diagnostic since the real spawn path (server-lifecycle.ts) is unaffected.

Use JSON.stringify to properly escape backslashes and quotes.

* openspec: propose fix-electron-extracted-jiti-and-stdio-capture

Two related Electron startup bugs found while debugging a Windows v0.4.6
install:

1. selectLaunchSource() returns kind=extracted with cliPath whose tree
   is degraded (jiti missing). spawnFromSource() then FATALs because
   resolveJitiFromAnchor returns null and the fallback resolveJitiImport
   uses process.argv[1] = electron.exe which cannot resolve jiti.
   Root: needsExtraction only checks .version marker, not tree health.

2. spawnDetached hard-codes stdio[1]='ignore', so child stdout never
   reaches logFd. Server log files end up 0 bytes on a clean startup,
   blinding diagnostics. server/cli.ts already does this correctly with
   raw spawn(); spawnDetached is the outlier.

Proposal adds:
- extractedSourceIsHealthy(cliPath) pure helper + wiring to force
  re-extract when marker matches but tree is degraded.

* build(electron): pin appdmg + fail fast on incompatible Node versions

When building the macOS DMG locally on Node 25, the Electron build failed
deep inside electron-forge with 'Cannot find module appdmg'. Two contributing
gaps:

  1. `appdmg` is an *optional* transitive dep of `electron-installer-dmg`
     (used by `@electron-forge/maker-dmg`). On certain npm runs it gets
     skipped silently, leaving DMG building broken with no upfront signal.

  2. `appdmg` itself depends on `macos-alias`, a native module that does
     not compile on Node 25 (V8 internal API changes). Today this surfaces
     only when the user runs `npm run electron:build` — too late and too
     opaque.

Fixes:

  - Add `appdmg` to root `optionalDependencies` so npm always attempts
    the install rather than skipping it as a deep transitive optional.
  - Add root `engines.node` (`>=22.12.0 <25`) — `<25` excludes the
    macos-alias-incompatible Node 25 line. Documented prerequisite in
    docs/faq.md is already "Node.js 22.12+", so this codifies it.
  - Add `.npmrc` with `engine-strict=true` so a fresh `npm install` on
    Node 25 fails fast with EBADENGINE rather than silently skipping
    optional `appdmg` and erroring at `electron-forge make` time.

Verified:

  - Node 22.22.2: `npm install` succeeds, `node_modules/appdmg/` present.
  - Node 25.8.1: `npm install --dry-run` errors with `EBADENGINE` — fail fast.

Discovered while running the local Intel macOS DMG build for the
`doctor-rich-output` change. Build now completes cleanly to
`packages/electron/out/make/PI-Dashboard-darwin-x64-0.4.6.dmg` (156 MB).

  - Add the engines/Node guidance to docs/faq.md / electron-build-methods.md
    so future contributors hit the explicit error message before reaching

docs(openspec): replace JsonNullable PATCH with PUT contracts

Remove JsonNullable-dependent PATCH update contracts and replace them
with explicit PUT-only APIs to simplify serialization, OpenAPI
generation,
and client SDKs while preserving domain event behavior.

- Remove PATCH endpoints and JsonNullable request models to eliminate
  patch-specific serialization semantics
- Add PUT-only contracts for current-user profile, preferences, and
  meeting settings to enforce full-replacement semantics and explicit
  nullable handling (null clears)
- Update OpenAPI generation to regenerate the unified spec without PATCH
  operations or JsonNullable component schemas to produce nullable-free
  API artifacts
- Update Android OpenAPI generator and networking config to disable
  nullable wrappers and remove JsonNullableModule registration to
  regenerate SDKs that do not require JsonNullable
- Remove jackson-databind-nullable dependency and
  JsonNullableJackson3Module
  from backend shared config to simplify runtime configuration
- Migrate and add tests to reflect PUT semantics, explicit password
  handling,
  timeout clearing, and LIVE auto-approval behaviors to preserve
  integrity
- Add design, proposal, specs, tasks, verification, and report artifacts
  to
  document the migration plan and validation outcomes

BREAKING CHANGE: PATCH /api/v1/me, PATCH /api/v1/me/preferences, and
PATCH /api/v1/meetings/{id}/settings are removed; clients must use the
corresponding PUT endpoints and regenerate SDKs.

Signed-off-by: Nguyễn Ngọc Phú <ngocphunguyenabc@gmail.com>

commits.message:
feat(api): replace patch endpoints with PUT contracts

The patch-based partial-update flows using JsonNullable added complexity
and
special-case handling. Replacing them with explicit PUT full-replace
contracts
simplifies request handling, removes the JsonNullable dependency, and
makes
password and preferences semantics explicit.

- Add PutMeetingSettingsCommand and PutMeetingSettingsUseCase to enable
  full
  replacement of meeting settings via PUT
- Add MeetingSettingsPasswordResolver to normalize raw passwords and
  compute
  hashes when replacing settings
- Add PutMeetingSettingsUseCaseTest to exercise PUT-based meeting
  settings flows
- Remove UpdateMeetingSettingsCommand, UpdateMeetingSettingsUseCase,
  UpdateMeetingSettingsRequest and related JsonNullable patch DTOs to
  drop the
  PATCH-based flow
- Update MeetingController and presentation DTOs to accept PUT-based
  settings
  requests to align the API surface with full-replace semantics
- Add PutPreferencesCommand, PutUpdatePreferencesUseCase and
  UserPreferencesSerializer to replace preference merge-patch with
  explicit
  replacement and JSON serialization
- Refactor user profile update to replaceProfile and adjust AvatarUpdate
  variants
  to reflect full-profile replacement intent
- Remove JsonNullableJackson3Module configuration and drop
  jackson.databind.nullable from several service build files to
  eliminate the
  JsonNullable transitive requirement
- Add CommonErrorCode.METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED and expand
  GlobalExceptionHandler
  imports to handle additional web error cases

BREAKING CHANGE: Several PATCH endpoints and JsonNullable-based request
DTOs were
removed and replaced by PUT full-replace endpoints (meeting settings and
user
preferences/profile). Clients must switch to the new PUT APIs and update
request
bodies/semantics accordingly.

Signed-off-by: Nguyễn Ngọc Phú <ngocphunguyenabc@gmail.com>

feat(user-management): add profile patching, queries, events

Enable partial profile updates, profile queries, and event publishing so clients
can manage profiles and downstream services can maintain local projections
without HTTP callbacks.

- Add PatchUserRequest and PatchPreferencesRequest DTOs to represent
  JsonNullable-based patch payloads
- Add PATCH /api/v1/users/me and PATCH /api/v1/users/me/preferences endpoints to
  support partial profile and per-field preference updates
- Add GetUserUseCase, GetUsersSliceUseCase and controller GET endpoints to
  expose /users/me, /users/{id}, and /users with slice pagination and filters
- Introduce UserUpdatedEvent and register it in User.updateProfile to notify
  downstream services of profile changes
- Update User aggregate and repository to handle profile updates and to support
  findActiveUsers returning paginated slices
- Update UserPreferencesParser, add UserPreferencesResponse and update
  Login/Refresh/Preferences use cases to return output DTOs to separate
  input/output contracts
- Update JacksonConfig and build.gradle to register JsonNullableJackson3Module
  and add jackson-databind-nullable dependency to enable JsonNullable support
- Add JPA query (findActiveFiltered) and adapt UserRepositoryAdapter to map
  Slice to PageResult to enable filtered slice queries
- Add unit and integration tests to validate profile patching, preference
  merging, queries, and event publishing

Signed-off-by: Nguyễn Ngọc Phú <ngocphunguyenabc@gmail.com>

refactor(shared): reorganize shared package namespace and errors

Standardize shared package layout and centralize web error handling to avoid
naming collisions and improve cross-service reuse.

- Remove legacy domain and web classes to migrate to namespaced layout
- Add namespaced ValueObject to provide a canonical shared domain interface
- Add CommonErrorCode to centralize infra-level error codes across services
- Add ErrorCode marker interface to unify service-specific error enums
- Add GlobalExceptionHandler to map validation and unexpected exceptions to
  JSend
- Update violation code resolution to normalize constraint codes to
  ViolationCode

Signed-off-by: Nguyễn Ngọc Phú <ngocphunguyenabc@gmail.com>

# Tasks: webhook-to-ci-job

> Implementation tasks từ `proposal.md` + `specs/review-job/spec.md` + `design.md`.
> Strict TDD (config.yaml): logic tasks = RED → GREEN → TRIANGULATE → REFACTOR.

## Review Workload Forecast

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Estimated changed lines | ~1200 (additions ~600 + deletions ~600) |
| 400-line budget risk | High |
| Chained PRs recommended | Yes (but coupling-limited — xem note) |
| Suggested split | PR1: core rewrite + removal (atomic) → PR2: docs/Dockerfile/template polish |
| Delivery strategy | ask-on-risk |
| Chain strategy | feature-branch-chain |

```text
Decision needed before apply: Yes
Chained PRs recommended: Yes
Chain strategy: feature-branch-chain
400-line budget risk: High
```

**Note split:** `config.ts` + `repo.ts` shared giữa webhook code (cũ) và CI path (mới) →
khó tách "additive PR1 + removal PR2" sạch (sửa `repo.ts`/`config.ts` break compile
webhook.ts). Đề xuất: **PR1 = core rewrite + removal atomic** (compile green cuối),
**PR2 = docs/Dockerfile/template** (low-risk polish). Hoặc single-PR với commit atomic
per-layer nếu user chấp nhận review lớn.

Wrap try/catch→`ReviewOutcome`. **RED** `test/review.test.ts` (rewrite từ `webhook.test.ts`): approve→ok:0, request_changes→ok:0, inconclusive→fail, exception→fail (mock gitlab/pi). **GREEN** impl.

commits.message:
feat(ci): CI wait mode + cancel-stale-review + skills doc (#1)

Adds opt-in CI wait mode so the bot defers review until the GitLab pipeline
for the reviewed commit passes, plus fixes for the multi-pipeline and
re-push races that the new mode surfaces. Also adds the daily-workflow
skills doc and an in-flight coordinator that cancels a stale review when a
newer push arrives.

## Features

- ci.require (opt-in via .pi/config.yaml): bot waits for CI success before
  reviewing, listens to pipeline webhooks, and skips review on failed/
  canceled/ skipped pipelines. Per-project ci.waitTimeoutMs overrides the
  CI_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS env default.
- Pipeline webhook handler in index.ts consumes pending entries keyed by
  projectId:sha to trigger deferred reviews.

## Bug fixes

- BUG 1 (stale CI wait on re-push): secondary mrIid->sha index in ciwait.ts
  clears the previous pending entry when a new push arrives, so a pipeline
  webhook for the old SHA can no longer trigger a stale review.
- BUG 2 (multi-pipeline aggregate): getMrPipelineStatus now filters
  pipelines by SHA and aggregates status across all of them (any running
  wins, all-success required), so a failing branch pipeline is no longer
  masked by a successful MR pipeline.
- BUG 3 (two reviews racing on re-push): new inflight.ts registers each
  review by projectId:mrIid and aborts the previous session via
  AbortSignal when a newer push supersedes it; performReview swallows the
  AbortError silently so the newer review owns the verdict.

## UX

- checkCiAndWait de-duplicates the 'Đợi CI pass' note per SHA via
  listMrComments, avoiding note spam when devs push repeatedly while CI is
  running.

## Observability

- /healthz and /stats expose ciWait.pending and reviewsActive counts.

## Docs

- docs/SKILLS.md: daily workflow skills for developers/AI agents using a
  project that already has the bot set up (read notes, decode verdicts,
  re-trigger, debug 'bot im lặng').
- docs/CONFIG.md, INTEGRATION.md, SETUP.md, ARCHITECTURE.md,
  MULTIPROJECT.md, AGENTS.md, README.md: document the ci schema, re-push
  behavior, D10/D11 decisions, and link cross-repo references to GitHub
  URLs.
- All doc references converted to absolute GitHub URLs.

## Tests

- 65 tests pass (was 22). Adds regressions for mergeConfig ci.* fields,
  resolveCiWaitTimeoutMs priority, ciwait pending lifecycle (incl. BUG 1
  re-push clear), aggregatePipelineStatus multi-pipeline cases (BUG 2),
  and inflight coordinator lifecycle (BUG 3).

Co-authored-by: Nai Coi <naicoi@gmail.com>

the openspec init upgrade and supporting tooling.

## Changes authored

1. `adopt-design-md-format` (53 tasks, 2 capability deltas)
   - New capability `design-system-format`: file location, frontmatter token
     coverage, lint gate via `@google/design.md` CLI, section order, precedence,
     spec context cache, OKLCH↔hex parity (auto-derived, lint-enforced),
     liveness probe (weekly cron probes upstream archive + staleness +
     fixture-snapshot behavior tests).
   - `style-system` ADD: Token Traceability to DESIGN.md (error severity,
     allow-listed orphans).
   - Adopts google-labs-code/design.md (Apache-2.0, alpha) format with exact
     version pin, signed-tarball install via `npm ci --ignore-scripts`,
     pinned upstream commit SHA + LICENSE-file SHA in docs.

2. `update-site-marketing-redesign` (94+ tasks, 9 capability deltas)
   - REDESIGN of `/`, `/platform`, `/roadmap`; ADD `/use-cases`, `/standards`,
     `/writing`, `/writing/[slug]`, `/writing/feed.xml`.
   - `style-system` MODIFIED + ADD: cascade layers, fluid type via clamp(),
     container-query primitives, self-hosted WOFF2 with metrics overrides,
     font payload budget (≤180 KB/route, ≤60 KB/family), LCP preload pin
     (Space Grotesk for marketing routes), token categories, midnight theme
     alongside twilight, Lighthouse CI perf gate at error severity (perf ≥0.9,
     CWV asserts), merge-order prerequisite gate, existing-token preservation,
     Card Variant Set (split from MODIFIED Solid Card Variant per review).
   - `site-content` MODIFIED: route inventory, frontmatter contract,
     canonical taglines single source, code examples per pillar, latest-writing
     module, type-safe schemas extended.
   - `site-navigation` ADD: primary nav, skip link with focus-move, mobile
     hamburger, footer, theme toggle with aria-pressed + safe pre-paint
     bootstrap, CSP inline-script hash drift gate, BaseLayout slot ABI
     (json-ld/indexation/branding) so 4 caps don't shotgun-edit BaseLayout.
   - `site-standards-registry` ADD: typed registry, `StandardChip`/`StandardsRow`,
     single-source consumption, DefinedTerm JSON-LD, `:focus-visible` caption
     for keyboard-only desktop.
   - `site-bridge-story` ADD: canonical sentence + variants allow-list,
     accessible SVG flow, hero CTA `/platform#bridge`, 301 redirect to
     `/platform` (no fragment, preserves PageRank), same-origin redirect
     enforcement.
   - `site-mobile-layout` ADD: 3-breakpoint contract, no global viewport scale,
     tap targets ≥44×44 enumerated for chips/icon-buttons/hamburger/tooltip
     close/theme toggle, TrustChain tooltip a11y (role=dialog, Esc dismiss,
     reduced-motion opacity-only ≤80ms), TrustChain reduced-motion freeze on
     end-state, non-color signal for PERMIT/DENY, forced-colors sitewide.
   - `site-structured-data` ADD: Organization+WebSite (no SearchAction while
     /search noindex), Article+BreadcrumbList with publisher required, JSON-LD
     `</script>` injection escape + size budget (≤8 KB/route).
   - `site-indexation` ADD: NOINDEX_ROUTES single source, sitemap `<lastmod>`
     from MDX frontmatter (not CI mtime), robots.txt, RSS link rel=alternate,
     trailing-slash policy.
   - `site-branding` ADD: favicons, theme-color per scheme, web manifest,
     per-slug OG images, inline-wordmark ban.

3. `add-brand-assets-and-writing-pipeline` (52 tasks, 4 capability deltas)
   - New capability `site-brand-gallery`: `/brand` route renders all 13
     DESIGN.md §4.14 variants (6 glyphs incl. bold for ≤32px, 2 wordmarks,
     3 avatars, 2 OG cards), copy-SVG buttons with no-JS fallback, noindex,
     relaxed Lighthouse perf threshold (≥0.8).
   - New capability `site-writing-pipeline`: build-time GitHub clone with
     SHA-pinned sequence (NOT `git clone --branch <SHA>`, which is invalid),
     hardened `repository_dispatch` webhook (hardcoded repo, sha allowlist
     verified via `git ls-remote`, ref argument-injection guard, concurrency
     group), MDX component allowlist (AST-enforced via remark plugin —
     Astro's built-in `components` config does NOT enforce), SHA-pinned
     "View source on GitHub" link, end-to-end merge-to-visible latency
     P95 ≤10 min with `<meta name="artagon:build-sha">` and PR status check,
     graceful local-only fallback with zero-post empty-state.
   - `site-content` MODIFIED: `Per-route Frontmatter Contract` extended with
     `repo` (Zod allowlist), `path`, `commit` (40-hex), `cover` regex
     (SSRF guard against absolute URLs hitting metadata endpoints),
     future-dated posts excluded without build error.

     `src/data/brand-svgs.ts` (typed factory using `as const satisfies`),
     multi-surface inline-glyph ban (CSS data: URIs + Astro raw blocks +
     alt viewBoxes), no-external-href in SVG factory (sharp/librsvg SSRF
     guard), DESIGN.md §4.14 glyph parity with coordinated-update CI gate,
     static OG default with per-slug satori override composition.

Each change went through parallel multi-dimension adversarial review:
- adopt-design-md-format: 4 dims (architecture, supply-chain, DX, openspec
  authoring) → 11 must-fix → all addressed → round-2 verification:
  AMENDMENTS-COMPLETE.
- update-site-marketing-redesign: 5 dims (security, accessibility,

Fix API base URL, correct field names, add e2e tests

Major discovery: the Watermelon API uses /api/v1 prefix (not /),
and field names differ from what was assumed (email_address not email,
first_name/last_name not name, etc). Webhook API uses action_id/
entity_id/verb_id (not event strings) and doesn't support GET listing.

- Fix BASE_URL to https://public.watermelon.ai/api/v1
- Rewrite contacts tools: email_address (required), first_name,
  last_name, telephone_number, location
- Rewrite search: fieldValue + optional fieldId (not query string)
- Rewrite webhooks: action_id/entity_id/verb_id params, remove
  nonexistent list endpoint
- Rewrite messages: payload field, user_id param
- Add Field() validators for schema-visible bounds
- Improve all tool docstrings for LLM self-description
- Add e2e test suite: 12 tests (10 pass, 2 skip for conversations
  which need a chatbot configured)
- Handle API response shapes (list wrapping, 204 no-content)

Initial commit: MCP server for Watermelon.ai (13 tools)

TypeScript MCP server wrapping the full Watermelon public API:
contacts (5), conversations (2), messages (2), fields (1), webhooks (3).
Includes gap analysis and OpenSpec artifacts.

Escapes per spec.md Requirement "Typed escape-on-construction prevents Swift code injection from user data": `"` → `\"`, `\` → `\\`, `\n` → `\\n`, `\r` → `\\r`, `\t` → `\\t`, control chars 0x00-0x1F and 0x7F → `\\u{<hex>}`, U+2028 / U+2029 → `\\u{2028}` / `\\u{2029}`. **Behavior**: input `'A\\B"C'` produces output `'A\\\\B\\"C'` (R-string repr; the underlying bytes match what Swift expects in source). **Verify**: `swift test --filter test-escape.R` (test in §6.1) passes.

refactor(sruth): move sruth/ → docs/sruth/ (the pre-v4 subtree)

Per the user's plan: `sruth/` (61MB legacy pre-v4 sub-project
tree) is moved to `docs/sruth/` where it joins the other
documented history (`docs/agents/`, `docs/dagster/`,
`docs/INTEGRATIONS_INDEX.md`, etc.).

The move uses `git mv` with rename detection; `.gitignore` was
updated to point at the new path. The `docs/sruth/oideachais/notebooks/**/
__marimo__/session/` exclusion pattern is preserved.

**Why this change:**

After the 2026-07-17 v7 flattening (commit `2026-07-17-v7-flatten-\ncianfhoghlaim-merge-bonneagar-rewrite-readme-license-v1`),\nthe `sruth/` subtree was retained as a separate legacy tree.
The decision was: `sruth/` would be deprecated but kept
in-tree for historical reference. Now that:

- The cianfhoghlaim core has stabilized (Mega-3 a/b/c all
  committed)
- The agent fleet has consolidated (15 agents in AGENT_REGISTRY)
- The web monorepo + integration runtimes are wired

…the sruth/ subtree is fully legacy and should live alongside
the other documented-history artifacts (`docs/CHOP_AND_CHANGE_GUIDE.md`,
`docs/FAMILY_HISTORY.md`, etc.) rather than at the repo root.

**Net changes:**

- 3139 renames: `sruth/<path>` → `docs/sruth/<path>`
- 4 .gitignore updates: `sruth/oideachais/...` → `docs/sruth/...`
- 1 sruth/oideachais/notebooks/__marimo__/session pattern updated

This is the move-only commit. The bulk cocoindex-flows sweep of\ndocs/sruth/ is deferred — the docs/ tree is documentation, not\nactive code, so the rename applies only to reference docs (which\nmostly correctly say 'cocoindex_flows' already — only 5–10\nreferences remained drifted in sruth/).

anchor_commit_observation.message:
fix(client): restore mdiConsoleLine import + add chrome ErrorBoundary

Spawning a new session in the Electron app blanked the entire window
(incl. titlebar, app frozen) until reload. Root cause: commit 26cc9ee7
removed mdiConsoleLine from the @mdi/js import in SessionCard.tsx but
left two `?? mdiConsoleLine` fallbacks behind. Existing sessions all
carry known sources, so the dangling reference stayed cold; a freshly
spawned session with a source missing from sourceIcons evaluated the
fallback and threw `ReferenceError: mdiConsoleLine is not defined`
during render. The throw bubbled past the layout chrome (no
ErrorBoundary above the inner ChatView one at App.tsx:1117), unmounting
the entire React tree.

Three layers of fix:

1. Restore the missing import in SessionCard.tsx (one-line).
2. Wrap apiProvider's children in a top-level <ErrorBoundary> so any
   future render-time throw in chrome (sidebar, session list, content
   header, MobileShell) degrades to a recoverable 'Shell encountered an
   error' panel + Reload button instead of blanking the window. Inner
   ChatView boundary still wins for chat-only errors via React's
   nearest-boundary semantics.

commits.message:
feat(cron): universal redacted visibility + shared (editableByAnyone) scheduled messages

Every channel-targeted scheduled job is now visible to everyone: full rows
for the owner/admins/shared jobs, identity-and-schedule-only redacted rows
otherwise; DM-targeted and channelless personal jobs stay invisible to
non-owners on every read path. A new editableByAnyone flag (skills
precedent) opens edit/disable/run-now — never delete — to everyone; the
flag itself stays owner/admin. update_scheduled_message gains an enabled
field so 'turn off' can disable instead of delete, and cancel confirms its
target by name. Access control is centralized in src/tools/cronJobAccess.ts.
Home Tab Skills and Schedules regroup into Shared / Yours / Non-Accessible
sections with a shared-flag toggle, and 'editable by everyone' is renamed
'shared' everywhere.

feat(plugins): SDK reconcileCronJobs + watchFile for plugin-owned schedules

Declarative API a plugin calls during init: diff against existing
plugin === ownerKey jobs, upsert entries in specs[], delete prior
owner-jobs not in specs[]. Preserves the admin-toggled enabled flag.
Adds plugin-scoped watchFile (closed on plugin reload to avoid
cross-generation double-fires) and wires data/config.json into the
existing config watcher so plugins observe config changes for free.

CronJob gains pluginManaged/specKey for stable identity across
reconciles; update_scheduled_message / cancel_scheduled_message refuse
plugin-managed jobs. Home Tab splits the Scheduled Messages section
into user-created (full controls) and plugin (read-only +
Enable/Disable, admin-only).

build: add oxlint, oxfmt, and lefthook for linting and formatting

- Add oxlint with typescript/import/unicorn plugins and deny-warnings
- Add oxfmt formatter and establish clean baseline across all src/ files
- Configure lefthook pre-commit hook (lint, format, test in parallel)
- Add VS Code extension recommendation for oxc-vscode
- Fix all lint warnings (unused imports, useless fallbacks, etc.)
- Add tsconfig.build.json to exclude test files from production build

feat: add cron-based scheduled messages with silentThinking mode

Cron scheduler that ticks every 60s and executes matching jobs via
processMessage. Dynamic jobs spawn a Claude session; responses are
posted as top-level channel messages (silentThinking bypasses the
streaming UX).

Includes CRUD tools (create/cancel/update/list_scheduled_messages),
Home Tab management UI, resolveChannelId helper extracted from 3
tools, TriggerType extended with "scheduled", and delivery context
for non-interactive execution.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style: fix go fmt in provider.go

* docs: add missing generated docs for kibana_dashboard and kibana_stream

* fix(docs): remove kibana_dashboard and kibana_stream docs to prevent check-docs CI failures

* chore(openspec): archive es-entitycore-migration-phase2-logstash via verify-openspec

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: trigger checks

* fix(provider): remove migrated SDKv2 resources from old provider

The ingest_pipeline and logstash_pipeline resources were migrated to
Plugin Framework entitycore envelope but were still referenced in the
legacy SDKv2 provider, causing build failures. They are already
registered in the Plugin Framework provider (provider/plugin_framework.go).

* fix(models): remove omitempty from LogstashPipeline description

The description field needs to be sent as empty string to the API
when cleared by the user, so that Elasticsearch properly unsets it.
With omitempty, the empty string was omitted from the PUT payload,
causing the old description value to persist server-side. This was
 causing TestAccResourceLogstashPipelineOptionalUnset to fail.

* fix(entitycore): update schema factory signatures to accept context.Context

Updates the schema factory functions to match the new entitycore
NewElasticsearchResource/NewElasticsearchDataSource signatures that
now require func(context.Context) schema.Schema.

Fixes build failures caused by origin/main introducing the signature
change without updating all callers.

* fix(logstash): add defaults for description and username to match SDKv2 behavior

Adds stringdefault.StaticString("") to description and
stringdefault.StaticString("api_key") to username so that:
1) Removing description from config sends an empty string to the API
   (clearing the field), matching the old SDK behavior.
2) username defaults to "api_key" when not specified, preserving
   backward compatibility with the old SDKv2 DefaultFunc.

Fixes TestAccResourceLogstashPipelineOptionalUnset acceptance test.

* fix(logstash): revert incorrect defaults and omitempty removal, fix test expectation

Reverts the recent attempts to fix TestAccResourceLogstashPipelineOptionalUnset by:

- Removing Default modifiers from description and username (they were introducing drift)

- Restoring omitempty on LogstashPipeline.Description

- Updating the test to reflect actual Elasticsearch behavior: the API retains description when omitted from config

The previous fixes (commits 769c8be6 and 7d4a24c7) were based on an incorrect assumption that Elasticsearch clears the description field when an empty string is sent. CI across all ES versions shows the API preserves the existing value.

* fix(logstash): use jsontypes.NormalizedType for pipeline_metadata and add SDK->PF migration test

- Switch pipeline_metadata schema attribute from plain StringAttribute to
  jsontypes.NormalizedType for proper JSON normalization.
- Update Data.PipelineMetadata field from types.String to jsontypes.Normalized.
- Update readLogstashPipeline to use jsontypes.NewNormalizedValue when
  setting pipeline_metadata in state.
- Add TestAccResourceLogstashPipelineMigration acceptance test that creates
  a pipeline with the legacy SDKv2 provider (v0.14.5) via ExternalProviders
  and then verifies seamless migration to the Plugin Framework provider.

Addresses review comments on PR #2750.

## Phase 1 amendment — active banner-grab phase in sweep service

This amendment adds an opt-in active banner-grab phase to the
existing **sweep service** (`go/pkg/scan/`, NOT the SNMP/API-focused
mapper at `go/pkg/mapper/`). The phase runs after the SYN half-open
scanner identifies live `(host, port)` pairs and emits
`BannerObservation` records that the agent forwards to netprobe in
bounded batches over a new `MatchBanners` IPC method. Netprobe matches
the supplied observations against the §32 Recog / Satori corpora and
returns labels; the agent emits or forwards the resulting
`FingerprintEvent`s. No corpus duplication, no shared Rust/Go crate, no
cgo. Banner grab is a streaming enrichment pipeline over SYN-confirmed
open ports, not a second in-memory scanner; preserve the SYN half-open
scanner's large-inventory latency profile while allowing exhaustive
active probing when operators choose that trade-off. HTTPS/TLS evidence
stays in the passive TLS/SSL fingerprint pipeline rather than active
HTTPS decryption. See `design.md` D16 for the architectural rationale.
